smell: The canonical slog wiring ships NopLogger and tui.SimpleLogger with no redacting middleware. Every slog.Handler in the process (stdout, stderr, and the optional --log-file multi-writer) sees raw values, so a future caller that passes a ProxmoxCredentials or a []byte password as a slog attr leaks it to stdout/stderr/logfile. Security owns the policy finding; observability owns the sink: there is no redact.Handler wrapping charmlog output.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — no preventative redaction layer in a privilege-sensitive tool; downgraded from blocker because no current log site demonstrates a leak, but installing the guard before a regression occurs is the point.
fix_summary: Add an internal/logutil/redact package with a Handler wrapper that walks slog.Record attrs, matches values of type credentials.ProxmoxCredentials / []byte named password/token/secret / *url.URL with user-info set, and rewrites them to ***. Install it in tui.buildLogger (wraps charmlog) and in tui.SimpleLogger (wraps dualHandler). Gate via a UnitTest that logs a ProxmoxCredentials and asserts the sink output never contains the secret. Pair with Seam #3 errors-side redaction so both chain and sink are covered.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets
repo-counter-example: internal/tui/wizard/components/input.go:L131 — strings.ReplaceAll(f.err.Error(), value, "***") is the hand-rolled version this handler would generalize
Seam #3 (observability owns the sink half)
must_preserve: internal/logutil.NopLogger as the canonical no-op — wrap, don't replace.

smell: The slog sink stringifies an error with `m.logger.Warn(err.Error())` — zero structured fields, so any future redacting handler (see obs:bbc23e42) cannot inspect the error chain for a credential-bearing typed error. This is the canonical repo pattern the prior-wave errors audit (err:7b2829bb) flagged at the error-type layer; the sink side is this audit.
severity_reason: rubric §4/un-idiomatic-pattern-that-has-bitten-the-repo-before — the errors wave already logged the mirror finding at the chain layer; the sink compounds it by losing structured inspection.
fix_summary: Replace `m.logger.Warn(err.Error())` with `m.logger.Warn("addon install failed", "addon", info.Name, "err", err)`. Add the same shape at the 2 other occurrences (artifacts.go:36, cli/root.go:90). Once the redacting handler exists, `"err", err` lets it walk the chain for a credentials-bearing typed error. Mirror the `msg + err` contract errors-side uses.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: pass errors structured via slog.Any or a string-key attr, not stringified
repo-counter-example: internal/version/updatecheck.go:L71 — slog.Debug("update check fetch failed", "err", err)
Seam #3 — observability owns the sink side
must_preserve: The error message text — callers read these at the terminal.

smell: Repository-wide pattern: 86+ call sites use `logger.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("foo: failed to X: %v", err))` instead of `logger.Warn("foo: failed to X", "err", err)`. This folds the error into the message string, so (a) any future redacting Handler cannot see the error as a separate attr and apply errors.As to scrub credentials, (b) JSON output (--log-format json) has no `err` field for log pipelines to index on, (c) the %v collapses typed-error structure the errtypes layer spent effort to preserve.
severity_reason: rubric §4/un-idiomatic-pattern — pervasive (~86 sites); blocks the redacting-handler fix (obs:bbc23e42) from being effective, and degrades --log-format json to unstructured message-string search.
fix_summary: Sweep the ~86 `fmt.Sprintf("...: %v", err)` log sites to structured form `logger.Warn("...", "err", err)`. Keep human-readable message prefix; move variable data (service, pkg, port, filename) to attrs. Cross-refs: dns/dnsmasq.go:188,195,199,211; firewall/firewall.go:152; cleanup/packages.go:21,77; cleanup/services.go:21,29,39,63,143,156; setup/apache.go:35,39,53,58,76,83; setup/artifacts.go:118,178; setup/haproxy.go:114,119,124,155,164; setup/steps.go:212,267,295,343,347,362; install/monitor.go:80,106,116; install/flux.go:59,68,79,83; postinstall/update_ingress.go:145,196,215,243,248,259,389,396,516,522; postinstall/haproxy.go:26,32,38,42,51,53,55,82; postinstall/bootstrap.go:56; postinstall/steps.go:97; destroy/helpers.go:46; destroy/steps.go:38,40; phase/helpers.go:15; phase/iso_cleanup.go:215,222,226,233; addon/manager.go:60,73,154; addon/catalog/flux/flux.go:96,194,205; addon/catalog/secretstore/secretstore.go:57,134,137; okd/okd.go:124. Stage as a single mechanical PR once the redacting handler lands so both are done atomically.
rule_source: Go log/slog design doc — attrs enable handler-side redaction and index-friendly JSON
repo-counter-example: internal/version/updatecheck.go:L71, L76 — correct structured form
Seam #3
must_preserve: Human-readable message prefix and contextual variable names.

smell: The codebase uses a `prefix: message` convention in the message string (e.g. 'terraform:', 'bootstrap:', 'haproxy:', 'cluster:', 'update-ingress:', 'kubevip:') but this prefix is NOT a structured attr — it is concatenated into the message body. When --log-format json is selected, a consumer cannot filter by `component=haproxy` because there is no such field. The prefix should be a stable attr (e.g. `"component", "haproxy"`) applied once via logger.With() at phase-construction time.
evidence:
p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("update-ingress: dns updated — *.apps → %s, api.* → %s", appsIP, vip))
p.Log.Info("haproxy: verifying api reachable via vip after teardown")
logger.Info("cleanup: haproxy service and configuration")
// No shared `component` attr; prefix only lives in the message string.
severity_reason: Pervasive field-stability issue — blocks JSON log filtering by component but no correctness risk.
fix_summary: At each phase constructor (setup, install, postinstall, destroy, cleanup) wrap the logger: `p.Log = logger.With("phase", "install")`. At sub-component boundaries (haproxy, dns, kubevip, terraform, iso, packages) further narrow with `logger.With("component", "haproxy")`. Then drop the `haproxy:` prefix from the messages, or keep it for TTY readability and rely on the attr for JSON. The dualHandler already propagates WithAttrs, so this composes. Update charmlog styles if needed.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: stable keys, per-component WithAttrs
Google SRE, Structured Logging chapter — 'fields are for machines, messages for humans'
repo-counter-example: cli/helpers.go:L153 — `tui.Info("starting deployment...", tui.LF("cluster", clusterFQDN))` is the correct shape, used once
must_preserve: Humans still read messages at the terminal; keep prefix in the TTY formatter.

smell: WaitFor logs `<prefix>: waiting for <description>... (N elapsed)` at Info level on every ticker tick (default 30s). Over a 30-minute bootstrap wait that is 60 identical Info lines per wait point; over the 60-minute install monitor it is 120. With ~5 concurrent polling call sites (kubevip daemonset, kubevip ping, kubevip api-health, haproxy api-via-vip, haproxy api-via-hostname, flux controllers, flux git sync) the Info stream drowns real state transitions. The 'waiting' line belongs at Debug; Info should fire once at start and once at ready.
severity_reason: Degrades signal-to-noise in operator-facing logs, but no correctness impact. Minor because the tick rate is 30s (not 1Hz), so the volume is bounded.
fix_summary: Downgrade the per-tick 'waiting...' line to logger.Debug. Keep the Info start/ready pair. If operator feedback matters on a slow TTY, emit Info at coarse intervals (e.g. every 5 minutes) by tracking a `lastNoticeAt` timestamp. Alternative: rely on the existing tui.StartSpinner at the caller for TTY feedback and keep the log sink silent between start and ready.
rule_source: Google SRE, Monitoring chapter: log state transitions, not heartbeat
Go log/slog idiom: Debug for heartbeat
must_preserve: The start log (waitMsg) and ready log (readyMsg) — operators rely on those.

smell: The Orchestrator runs StepDef items but does not emit a structured start/finish log pair per step. Skipping is logged (line 52) but success/duration is not — duration is captured in StepResult but never logged. Each phase individually decides whether to log 'X: starting Y'/'X: Y complete' in step.OnStart/OnComplete hooks (steps.go files do this sporadically), so operators see variable boundaries. For a long-running install (deploy > 60 min), missing duration per step hurts debuggability.
severity_reason: Debuggability gap — operators cannot see per-step durations without reading the final summary. Not a correctness risk.
fix_summary: In Orchestrator.executeStep, before step.OnStart() log `o.logger.Info("step started", "step", step.ID(), "name", step.Name())`. After step.OnComplete(), log `o.logger.Info("step completed", "step", step.ID(), "duration", duration)`. This gives every phase uniform span boundaries and removes the need for each steps.go to hand-roll start/end Info lines. Keep existing phase-level 'X: starting Y' lines in step.OnStart for TTY user-friendliness; the new structured lines are for JSON/file sinks.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries at orchestration layer
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/install/steps.go:L42-L45 — step OnStart manually logs 'bootstrap: waiting...' but not every step does, so boundaries are uneven
must_preserve: The existing hand-rolled OnStart/OnComplete lines that operators already rely on; new structured lines are additive.

smell: configureLogging does not auto-select JSON format when stdout is not a TTY. Operators piping `okdctl deploy | jq .` get charmlog text with ANSI color escapes by default and must know to pass `--log-format json`. Progress-bar suppression IS TTY-aware (line 31-32) so the shape of the fix already exists; log format should follow the same pattern.
severity_reason: UX affordance, not correctness. Operators can pass --log-format json explicitly.
fix_summary: If the --log-format flag was NOT explicitly set (check cmd.Flags().Changed("log-format")) and stdout is not a TTY, default logFormat to "json". Alternatively auto-disable ANSI color (SetColorProfile(ascii)) on non-TTY while keeping text format. Charmlog supports both via buildLogger. The existing `progressBars` gate at line 31 is the template.
rule_source: CLI UX convention: auto-switch to machine format when piped
Go log/slog design: handler selection at main
repo-counter-example: cli/logging.go:L31 — the TTY-aware path already exists for progress bars
must_preserve: The explicit --log-format flag takes precedence over auto-detection.

smell: secretstore.Install logs a 9-line HOW-TO guide ('1. download credentials, 2. create a connect token, ...') via env.Logger.Warn when the user has not yet configured secret files. Warn is for recoverable degradation; this is user education. Structured log sinks (JSON / file) will record nine Warn entries that an alerting rule will interpret as nine distinct problems. This is noise that belongs at Info or — better — at the TUI layer (fmt.Println) rather than the structured log.
evidence:
env.Logger.Warn("secretstore: to set up 1password connect secrets:")
env.Logger.Warn("  1. download 1password-credentials.json from Settings > Automation in 1password.com")
env.Logger.Warn("  2. create a connect token and save it:")
// ... 7 more env.Logger.Warn lines
severity_reason: Level-discipline smell — Warn misused for help text. Not correctness.
fix_summary: Emit the first line 'no secret files found ... skipping' at Warn (that's the actual warning). Print the numbered instructions via tui.Info or a direct fmt.Println block — operator-facing setup guidance is TTY UX, not machine-oriented structured logging.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: Warn for recoverable degradation, Info for state, fmt for user UX
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/deploy.go:L140-L147 — similar setup hint uses tui.Info/tui.Warn split correctly
must_preserve: The help content itself — move it, don't lose it.

smell: Manager.InstallAll iterates ordered addons and on failure logs `m.logger.Warn(err.Error())` (loses err structure, see obs:7b2829bb) and `addons: rolling back X` (Info) then on rollback failure another Warn. There is no structured `phase=rollback` field, no `addon` key, and no `attempt` marker — the three log lines for a failed install are loosely coupled by proximity in time. An async JSON pipeline cannot join them. Emit `logger.Info("addon install failed", "addon", info.Name, "err", err, "phase", "rollback")` once.
severity_reason: Span-boundary smell plus the err-stringified issue — both addressed by the structured-attr sweep.
fix_summary: Replace the three lines with two structured entries: `logger.Warn("addon install failed", "addon", info.Name, "err", err)` and `logger.Info("addon rollback", "addon", info.Name)`; on rollback failure, `logger.Warn("addon rollback failed", "addon", info.Name, "err", unErr)`. Once redacting handler exists, the errors are safely structured.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: one record per event, fields carry dimensions
Seam #3
must_preserve: The rollback semantics and the Uninstall call.

smell: setup.installPackagesStep logs `packages: <pkg> not found` and `packages: <pkg> already installed` at Info level for every package — one Info line per package, which for a typical RHEL setup is ~8 lines BEFORE the real work begins. The 'already installed' outcome is a no-op; Info is for state transitions. This is the `level-info-should-debug` pattern.
severity_reason: Level-discipline — Info for no-op state checks. Not correctness.
fix_summary: Drop the per-package log lines entirely; emit a single Info line after the loop: `p.Log.Info("packages: scanned system packages", "missing", len(toInstall), "installed", len(cfg.Packages)-len(toInstall))`. Move the per-package trace to Debug if it is diagnostically useful.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: Debug for per-item trace, Info for per-batch state
must_preserve: The final 'all system packages already installed' line — that's the useful Info.

smell: coreos.go logs `coreos: found existing iso at X` or `coreos: iso already exists at X` in four distinct places (L59, L73, L143, L204). During a single setup run more than one of these can fire for the same iso, producing three nearly-identical Info lines. This is a log-once violation — the check is duplicated in code because the caller structure grew organically.
severity_reason: Signal-to-noise; same event logged multiple times per run.
fix_summary: Consolidate the 'iso already present' check into one helper with a single Info log site; return early. If the two variants (found vs already-exists) are semantically distinct, rename them so operators can tell them apart.
rule_source: Google SRE, Structured Logging: log-once-per-event
must_preserve: The diagnostic value — either variant needs to remain, but not both per event.

smell: The log message `update-ingress: dns updated — *.apps → %s, api.* → %s` embeds Unicode em-dash and right-arrow characters. In JSON output these survive (UTF-8) but break text grep pipelines that assume ASCII (`grep -- ->`). Multiple sites across the repo use → and — in messages (postinstall/steps.go:L87, update_ingress.go:L203). If the repo's JSON consumers index on message text, this is fine; if they grep, it is a trap.
evidence:
p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("update-ingress: dns updated — *.apps → %s, api.* → %s", appsIP, vip))
p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("dns: api.* → vip %s, *.apps → bastion %s (haproxy)", state.KubeVipIP, bastionIP))
severity_reason: Stylistic — no correctness impact. Only matters if downstream tooling is ASCII-only.
fix_summary: Replace em-dash with ` - ` and right-arrow with ` -> `. Alternative: move the IP mapping to structured attrs (`"apps_ip", appsIP, "api_ip", vip`) and drop the glyphs from the message entirely.
rule_source: ASCII-safe log messages (classic Unix convention)
Go log/slog idiom: structure for machines, glyphs for humans

smell: executor.Run only logs `+ <name> <args>` at Debug when Verbose is true — nothing at Info for terraform/oc commands that run for minutes. Cross-ref: the prior-wave subprocess audit (sub:4c092fce, sub:7b2829bb) flagged that terraform output is buffered through the executor with no progress feedback. Observability owns the streaming-discipline half: there is no `cmd started ... cmd completed (dur, exit)` span log, so a JSON sink sees nothing about a 15-minute terraform apply until it finishes (or doesn't).
severity_reason: Operator feedback gap — the spinner covers TTY users, but JSON/file sinks see no progress. Not a correctness risk.
fix_summary: At the start of executor.run() log `e.logger.Debug("exec started", "cmd", name, "args", args)` and after cmd.Run() log `e.logger.Debug("exec completed", "cmd", name, "exit", result.ExitCode, "duration", result.Duration)`. Keep at Debug so operators don't see it by default but JSON sinks do when --log-level=debug. Do NOT log stdout/stderr — that's the streaming discipline the subprocess audit flagged separately.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries
Seam with subprocess audit (sub:4c092fce)
must_preserve: The Verbose-gated `+ name args` Debug line (existing convention).

smell: proxmox.Provision logs provisioned-vm counts and per-vm IP lines via fmt.Sprintf into the message: `terraform: plan will create %d virtual machines`, `terraform: provisioned %d vms`, and `terraform: %s: %s` (name, ip). Structured consumers cannot index on `vm_count` or `vm_ip`. This is the same pattern as obs:00000001 but for non-error fields; calling it out separately because the fix is different (numeric fields and IP addresses deserve typed attrs, not string interpolation).
severity_reason: Field-stability — numeric/IP fields wedged into message string. Fix is additive to obs:00000001.
fix_summary: `p.logger.Info("terraform: plan calculated", "vm_count", totalNodes)`; `p.logger.Info("terraform: provisioned vms", "count", len(result.VMs))`; `p.logger.Info("vm provisioned", "name", vm.Name, "ip", vm.IPAddress)`. Consider using netip.Addr type for the ip attr so the JSON sink sees a string of the canonical form.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: typed attrs
Seam #3 (sink side of the structured-logging push)
must_preserve: The operator-visible 'terraform: ...' prefix for TTY users — handled via WithAttrs in obs:00000002.

smell: MonitorInstallation's CSR approval tick runs every CSRApprovalInterval (30s) for up to 60 minutes. On each tick: on error it Warns, on approved>0 it Infos with running total. The error case correctly logs every tick (diagnostic value) but consider: if the CSR endpoint is down for minutes the Warn stream can reach ~120 entries, all identical in cause. This is the log-per-retry pattern at Warn level.
severity_reason: Bounded at 2 Warns/minute, which is tolerable. Downgrade to suggestion because the diagnostic value during a prolonged CSR outage (you WANT to see repeated failures) has merit.
fix_summary: De-duplicate identical consecutive Warns via a `lastWarnErrMsg` tracker, or downgrade consecutive repeats to Debug after the first. Keep approved>0 Info as-is (state transition). Only apply if operator feedback reveals the Warn stream is truly noisy.
rule_source: Google SRE, Monitoring: log state changes, not constant failures
Go proverb: clear is better than clever (don't over-engineer without feedback)
must_preserve: The approved>0 Info line — operators rely on it.
